newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty crawl to slow when CPI at 13 pct - NBP.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty crawl to slow when CPI at 13 pct - NBP.

text.p: The National Bank of Poland President Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz said the bank would slow the zloty crawling devaluation rate from the current one percent per month after year-on-year inflation falls to 13 percent.

"First, we have to reduce inflation to 13 percent and then, the crawl should be reduced, not much, but reduced," Gronkiewicz-Waltz told Reuters on Thursday during an international investment conference.
The year-on-year inflation was at 19.5 percent in September, down from 21.6 percent in 1995. The government aims to slash inflation to 13 percent at the end of 1997.
But analysts see this as an ambitious goal as Poland would likely miss its 1996 target of 17 percent inflation under pressure from fast rising food prices and high oil prices.
The budget plan for 1996 originally assumed the average rate of the monthly zloty devaluation against a basket of western currencies at 0.9 percent monthly.
But the central bank has held the rate at one percent since it last cut it from 1.2 percent early in January.

Analysts have said further reductions in the devaluation rate would have an deflationary effect but that a resulting relative strengthening of the zloty could prove difficult because of a deteriorating trade balance.

Gronkiewicz-Waltz, who was speaking after addressing the conference, said she expected Poland to record a balanced current account with a merchandise trade gap this year but that a further widening of the trade deficit was likely in 1997.
"According to the government forecast the trade deficit will widen to $9 billion so the current account will also deteriorate although foreign investment migh help offset the trade gap," she said.
After the first eight months of this year Poland had a current account surplus of $48 million and a trade shortfall of $4.5 billion.
